summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the selected Latin and the supplied bounded comparison reports. Both preserve the conditions for life, the categorical warning, speaker attribution, wholehearted repentance, the Lord’s assessment, and the erasure of former sins. The singular “God’s servant” is a disclosed working selection supported by the supplied report, with the Latin plural explicitly retained as an alternative. The notes also disclose the boundary difference and the interpretation of the stone marks and filling-in clause. Reader-facing “servant” and contextual “repentance” follow current policy. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Acceptance is limited to these supplied texts and disclosures; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
